name: Webhook inboxes
tagline: Endpoints your app sends its own webhooks to, answering however you need to test its retries.
stands_in_for: HMAC-signed webhooks (t=…,v1=… and plain hex or base64)
point: its own port, so resets, hangs and empty replies are real

capabilities.title: Every delivery kept
capabilities.text: Headers, body, signature check, the answer given and every attempt of the same event, newest first.

capabilities.title: Answer as you choose
capabilities.text: Always 200, accept with 202, always an error, fail N times then succeed, fail a share, hang, reset or an empty reply.

capabilities.title: Retries per event
capabilities.text: fail_then counts per event id or per inbox, so each event fails 3 times and the attempts show the app's backoff.

capabilities.title: Delays and hangs
capabilities.text: Add a delay before answering, or hold the request: 35 s tests a 30 s client timeout.

capabilities.title: Signature checks
capabilities.text: t-v1-hmac-sha256, hmac-sha256-hex or hmac-sha256-base64, with a timestamp tolerance and a replay check on the event id.

capabilities.title: Secret rotation
capabilities.text: Set previous_secret: a delivery signed with the old secret is marked as such. reject_bad answers 401 like a strict customer.

capabilities.title: Traps for the client
capabilities.text: A redirect to a private address (SSRF), a 50 MB answer, or one byte a second: each recorded as passed or failed.

capabilities.title: Ephemeral inboxes
capabilities.text: A test or an agent makes an inbox that expires by itself (1 h by default); kept ones live in webhooks/inboxes.yaml.

callouts.title: Ephemeral inboxes
callouts.text: Made by a test or an agent; each shows when it expires and who made it.

callouts.title: Old secret
callouts.text: Signed with the previous secret: the app is still using it after rotation.

callouts.title: Duplicate
callouts.text: The same event id seen before: the app sent it twice.

callouts.title: Old timestamp
callouts.text: Signed, but the timestamp is outside the tolerance (5 min by default).

callouts.title: Signature
callouts.text: Which scheme, which secret, the timestamp age and whether the id is new.

callouts.title: Mode
callouts.text: Fail N times then succeed; also always 200, 202, error, a share, hang, reset or empty.

callouts.title: Count per event id
callouts.text: Each event fails 3 times, not the inbox as a whole.

callouts.title: Hang
callouts.text: Hold the request: 35 s tests a client that gives up at 30 s.

callouts.title: Traps
callouts.text: Private redirect, huge answer, slow answer: the app should not follow, should cap and give up.

callouts.title: Attempts
callouts.text: Each attempt of the last event and the gap before it: the app's backoff, measured.

provoke.name: Fail then succeed
provoke.what: Each event gets 500 three times, then 200

provoke.name: Always an error
provoke.what: Every delivery gets the status you pick

provoke.name: Hang
provoke.what: No answer until the app gives up

provoke.name: Empty reply
provoke.what: The connection closes without a byte

provoke.name: Private redirect
provoke.what: 302 to a loopback address: does the app follow?

provoke.name: Huge answer
provoke.what: A 50 MB body: does the app stop reading?

provoke.name: One byte a second
provoke.what: Does the app give up on a slow answer?

advantages.title: Retries you can measure
advantages.text: Request bins show the request; here every attempt of an event is grouped, so the backoff is visible.

advantages.title: Failures beyond 500
advantages.text: Hangs, resets, empty replies and traps need a real socket; the inbox has its own port for that.

advantages.title: Signatures checked for you
advantages.text: Scheme, secret, rotation, timestamp and replay are checked on every delivery, not by hand.

advantages.title: Nothing left behind
advantages.text: Ephemeral inboxes delete themselves, so parallel tests and agents never share a URL.

agent.prompt: Check that the app retries an order.completed webhook three times with backoff and signs it correctly.
